source with only its default changed to `full`; it is compared separately.

CR handling. The later run tests the repaired source, not a resampling of a
model response. An identical duplicate pre-fix invocation remains in ignored
local audit storage. The unavailable Python command during editing was a local
tooling issue, not a CLI failure; the edit was completed using Node.

snapshots of the real CLI; no local runtime/private-context files were copied.

there are no model calls, historical model instructions, policy conditions,
usage comparisons, or recovery claims. The baseline and ablations select
executable component behavior. Their failures alone are not evidence of
improvement: the table directly compares historical, prepared, and final
sources on identical tasks. The ablations remove Unicode preservation or CSV
escaping independently; order and string conversion remain in all variants.

synthetic regression cases cover column order, line endings, whitespace and
scalar conversion; they were inspected while fixing the code and are not
held-out validation. Seven cases do not establish general correctness or
workload frequency. Output is one ordered record, not a general CSV parser;
exact minimal quoting and one final LF are the acceptance contract. Alternate
CSV encodings that parse equivalently are outside that contract.
EOF
cat > eval/README.md <<'EOF'
# Reproduce CSV checks

Requires Node.js (recorded runs: v22.23.4), Git, and a writable OS temporary
directory. No packages, network, credentials, or model/provider access needed.
From the repository root:

```sh
node eval/run.mjs --replay eval/pre-fix-results.json
node eval/run.mjs --replay eval/results.json
node eval/run.mjs --run .local/fresh-results.json
```

Fresh output paths must not already exist. Replay regrades captured actual
stdout and exit observations, checks source/task hashes, and compares each
saved per-case rating. It does not execute a newer artifact or claim that an
old source hash matches the working tree. For manual review, inspect each
`observation`, its task's `expected`, and the `rating` in the JSON files.

Fresh runs freeze the current production `app.mjs`, historical Git source,
prepared default-only intermediate, cases, and conditions before execution.
They run temporary copies through the actual Node CLI with identical settings
and task inputs, interleaved by case. Source text and hashes are saved along
with runtime, runner hash, all outputs, and per-case failure reasons. Any
future production change requires a fresh run, not just replaying old scores.
Cases and conditions are in `cases.json` and `run.mjs`; the two development
cases are retained as diagnostics. There is no policy fixture or empty-policy
control because no model/policy experiment is performed.

The production grader is exact stdout equality plus successful exit. Its
self-tests run before either mode: correct output, reordered columns, removed
LF, whitespace transformations, extra LF, nonzero exit, spawn failure, and
semantically equivalent JS constructions executed by Node. No trimming or
stdout instrumentation can conceal changed bytes. Expected CSV strings are
explicit task data rather than outputs computed using the implementation.
Infrastructure failures are classified separately. Fresh runs fail on those
or current-default/full mismatches; expected baseline/ablation mismatches do
not make the runner fail. Saved failing observations remain replayable.

Sources and inputs here are public-safe synthetic data. Ignored `.local/`
records are not dependencies of replay or fresh execution. Do not publish
private runtime context or provider reasoning with results.
EOF

+    fs.rmSync(directory, {recursive: true, force: true});
+  }
+  const record = {runtime: process.version, historicalRevision,
+    runnerSha256: hash(fs.readFileSync('eval/run.mjs')), sources, cases,
+    casesSha256: hash(JSON.stringify(cases)), conditions, results};
+  fs.writeFileSync(filename, JSON.stringify(record, null, 2) + '\n', {flag: 'wx'});
+  for (const condition of conditions) {
+    const rows = results.filter(row => row.condition === condition.id);
+    console.log(`${condition.id}: ${rows.filter(row => row.rating.pass).length}/${rows.length}`);
+  }
+  if (results.some(row => row.rating.type === 'infrastructure' ||
+      (['current-default', 'full'].includes(row.condition) && !row.rating.pass)))
+    process.exitCode = 1;
